name: Vina Falls
shortDescription: A dramatic 40m waterfall near Ngaoundéré.
fullDescription: Located about 15 km from Ngaoundéré, the Vina River plunges roughly 40 meters into a natural rock amphitheater, forming one of the Adamawa region's most striking natural sights.
funFact: The falls form a distinctive arc shape as the water cascades over the rock formation.

name: Lamido's Palace of Ngaoundéré
shortDescription: Traditional palace of the Fulani Lamido (ruler).
fullDescription: This palace showcases traditional Fulani architecture and remains the ceremonial seat of the Lamido, the traditional ruler of Ngaoundéré.
funFact: The palace's decorated walls illustrate centuries-old Fulani architectural traditions.

name: National Museum of Yaoundé
shortDescription: Cameroon's national collection of art and history.
fullDescription: Housed in a former presidential palace, this museum showcases artifacts, traditional art, and exhibits spanning Cameroon's diverse cultural history.
funFact: The building itself was once the official residence of Cameroon's first president.

name: Reunification Monument
shortDescription: Iconic monument marking Cameroon's 1961 reunification.
fullDescription: This landmark sculpture in Yaoundé commemorates the 1961 reunification of French and British Cameroon into a single nation.
funFact: The monument's spiraling design symbolizes the two territories coming together as one.

name: Dja Faunal Reserve
shortDescription: UNESCO-listed rainforest reserve, one of Africa's largest and best-protected.
fullDescription: Almost entirely surrounded by the Dja River, this reserve protects vast untouched rainforest and is home to gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants.
funFact: Over 90% of the reserve remains undisturbed primary rainforest.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Lobéké National Park
shortDescription: Remote rainforest park known for forest elephants and lowland gorillas.
fullDescription: Part of the Sangha Trinational conservation complex, Lobéké protects dense rainforest and forest clearings (bais) where wildlife gathers.
funFact: Lobéké's forest clearings let visitors observe forest elephants and gorillas in open view — rare for rainforest terrain.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Waza National Park
shortDescription: Cameroon's premier safari destination.
fullDescription: One of Central Africa's best wildlife parks, Waza is home to elephants, lions, giraffes, and hundreds of bird species across open savanna.
funFact: Waza is not a zoo — animals roam freely across the savanna, making it a true wilderness safari experience.

name: Rhumsiki Peak
shortDescription: Dramatic volcanic rock spire in the Mandara Mountains.
fullDescription: This iconic volcanic plug rises sharply from the surrounding Kapsiki plateau, surrounded by traditional villages and stunning sunset views.
funFact: Rhumsiki's jagged volcanic landscape has made it one of Cameroon's most photographed natural sites.

name: Douala Maritime Museum
shortDescription: Museum dedicated to Cameroon's seafaring and port history.
fullDescription: Located in the historic Bonanjo district, this museum traces Douala's evolution as a major port city through artifacts, models, and exhibits on maritime trade.
funFact: The museum includes a pirogue (canoe) simulator that lets visitors experience traditional local boating.

name: Douala-Edéa Wildlife Reserve
shortDescription: Mangrove and forest reserve near Douala.
fullDescription: Covering roughly 160,000 hectares, this reserve protects mangrove wetlands and rainforest, home to elephants, primates, and sea turtles.
funFact: The reserve's mangroves provide a rare habitat for manatees along Cameroon's coast.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Benoué National Park
shortDescription: Savanna park along the Benoue River.
fullDescription: One of Cameroon's key protected areas, home to lions, elephants, hippos, and hundreds of bird species along the Benoue River floodplains.
funFact: The park is named after the Benoue River, a major tributary that eventually joins the Niger River in Nigeria.

name: Rey Bouba Palace
shortDescription: Historic royal palace of the Lamido of Rey Bouba.
fullDescription: One of northern Cameroon's most important traditional palaces, seat of the powerful Lamido (traditional ruler) of Rey Bouba.
funFact: Rey Bouba's Lamidat is one of the oldest and most influential traditional Fulani kingdoms in the region.

name: Bamenda Ring Road
shortDescription: Scenic 367 km highland loop through villages and volcanic lakes.
fullDescription: This famous circuit winds through the Northwest's grassfields, passing waterfalls, crater lakes, and traditional villages along the way.
funFact: The Ring Road passes near several volcanic crater lakes formed by the region's ancient volcanic activity.
openingHours: Accessible daily, best in dry season

name: Bafut Palace
shortDescription: Traditional palace of the Fon (king) of Bafut.
fullDescription: This historic royal compound is the seat of the Fon of Bafut, featuring traditional architecture and a small museum of royal artifacts.
funFact: Bafut's traditional kingdom structure has remained largely intact for centuries.

name: Lobé Falls
shortDescription: Rare waterfall that flows directly into the ocean.
fullDescription: Located just outside Kribi, the Lobé River cascades directly into the Atlantic Ocean — one of very few waterfalls in the world to do so.
funFact: Local Batanga fishermen still paddle traditional canoes right up to the base of the falls.

name: Campo Ma'an National Park
shortDescription: Rainforest park near the coast, rich in biodiversity.
fullDescription: This park protects dense equatorial rainforest along Cameroon's southern coast, home to gorillas, forest elephants, and over 300 bird species.
funFact: Campo Ma'an is one of the most biodiverse protected areas in Central Africa.
openingHours: Guided tours only, arrange in advance

name: Mount Cameroon
shortDescription: West Africa's highest peak and an active volcano.
fullDescription: Standing at 4,040 m, Mount Cameroon is a major trekking destination, with routes taking climbers through rainforest, grassland, and volcanic terrain to the summit.
funFact: Mount Cameroon is one of Africa's most active volcanoes, with its most recent eruption in 2000.
openingHours: Guided treks, register in Buea before climbing

name: Limbe Botanic Garden
shortDescription: One of Africa's oldest botanical gardens.
fullDescription: Founded in 1892, this coastal garden showcases hundreds of tropical plant species along the Atlantic shoreline.
funFact: The garden was originally established by German colonial botanists in the 19th century.

name: Foumban Royal Palace
shortDescription: Historic palace and museum of the Bamoun Kingdom.
fullDescription: Home to generations of Bamoun kings (Sultans), this palace complex includes a museum displaying royal artifacts, art, and centuries of Bamoun history.
funFact: The Bamoun Kingdom developed its own writing script in the early 20th century, still preserved in the palace archives.

name: Bandjoun Chefferie
shortDescription: Traditional Bamileke royal chiefdom and museum.
fullDescription: This royal compound showcases Bamileke traditional architecture, wood carvings, and a museum preserving the chiefdom's cultural heritage.
funFact: The chiefdom's main hall features intricately carved wooden pillars, a hallmark of Bamileke craftsmanship.

name: Lake Tison
shortDescription: A scenic crater lake near Ngaoundéré.
fullDescription: A wooded crater lake surrounded by highland scenery, Lake Tison is a popular stop for walking, viewpoints, and quiet nature outings near Ngaoundéré.
funFact: The lake covers roughly 12 hectares and sits in a volcanic crater.

name: Mbé Cliff
shortDescription: A dramatic rocky escarpment overlooking the Adamawa landscape.
fullDescription: The Mbé Cliff is a mountainous rocky escarpment surrounded by wooded savanna, with hiking routes and views toward Lake Mazeré.
funFact: The site has been developed with trails and visitor facilities for trekking.

name: Lake Pangnéré
shortDescription: A large natural lake near Tibati.
fullDescription: Lake Pangnéré is a broad natural depression lake closely linked to the life and traditions of the communities around Tibati.
funFact: Unlike many lakes in Adamawa, Pangnéré is a depression lake rather than a crater lake.

name: Source of the Sanaga
shortDescription: The source area of Cameroon's longest major river.
fullDescription: Near Meiganga, the Sanaga begins as the Djérem before flowing across Cameroon toward the Atlantic, making the site interesting for geography and nature enthusiasts.
funFact: The Sanaga basin covers a large part of Cameroon before the river reaches the Atlantic.

name: Tello Falls
shortDescription: A picturesque waterfall in the Vina area.
fullDescription: Tello Falls is a forest-framed cascade in the Adamawa highlands and is among the region's notable waterfall destinations.
funFact: The falls are one of several waterfalls around the Vina highlands.

name: Mayo-Dadi Falls
shortDescription: A lesser-known waterfall in the Vina area.
fullDescription: Mayo-Dadi Falls offers a quieter waterfall experience among the landscapes around Ngaoundéré and the Vina Department.
funFact: It is listed by Cameroon's Ministry of Tourism among Adamawa tourist sites.

name: Djoumbal Mountains
shortDescription: Mountain landscapes in the Mayo-Banyo area.
fullDescription: The Djoumbal Mountains offer rugged highland scenery, hiking possibilities, and views across one of Adamawa's most mountainous areas.
funFact: The site is officially listed among Adamawa's tourist attractions.

name: Lamidat of Tibati
shortDescription: Traditional palace and seat of the Lamido of Tibati.
fullDescription: The Lamidat of Tibati offers visitors a window into the region's traditional political and cultural heritage and Fulani royal traditions.
funFact: Lamidats remain important living institutions in northern and Adamawa Cameroon.

name: Mefou Primate Sanctuary
shortDescription: A protected forest sanctuary for primates near Yaoundé.
fullDescription: The Mefou Primate Sanctuary provides a forest setting for observing and learning about chimpanzees, monkeys, and other primates rescued or protected in Cameroon.
funFact: It is one of the best-known wildlife attractions close to Yaoundé.

name: Ebogo Ecotourism Site
shortDescription: A riverside ecotourism destination on the Nyong.
fullDescription: Ebogo offers canoe excursions, forest walks, river scenery, and community-based ecotourism along the Nyong River south of Yaoundé.
funFact: The site is designed around low-impact nature and community tourism.

name: Mvog-Betsi Zoological Garden
shortDescription: A zoological garden in Yaoundé.
fullDescription: Located in Yaoundé, the Mvog-Betsi zoological garden provides an urban opportunity to see native wildlife and learn about Cameroon's fauna.
funFact: It is one of the attractions listed by the Ministry of Tourism for the Centre Region.

name: Bois Sainte Anastasie
shortDescription: A green urban recreation area in Yaoundé.
fullDescription: Bois Sainte Anastasie is a wooded leisure area in the capital, suitable for a break from the city and for experiencing urban greenery.
funFact: The site appears in the Ministry of Tourism's Centre Region attraction listings.

name: Akok-Bekoe Caves
shortDescription: Natural caves in the Centre Region.
fullDescription: The Akok-Bekoe caves are among the natural attractions identified by the Cameroonian government for the Centre Region and offer a more adventurous alternative to Yaoundé's museums.
funFact: The caves are specifically highlighted in Cameroon's official regional tourism description.

name: Ottomo Forest Reserve
shortDescription: A protected forest area near Ngoumou.
fullDescription: The Ottomo forest reserve preserves a section of the Centre Region's forest landscape and is suited to nature-focused excursions with local guidance.
funFact: It is specifically cited by the government as a tourist attraction of the Centre Region.

name: Charles Atangana Monument
shortDescription: A monument connected to Yaoundé's early history.
fullDescription: The monument commemorates Charles Atangana, an important traditional leader of the Ewondo people and a major figure in the history of Yaoundé.
funFact: Charles Atangana is remembered as a prominent chief associated with Yaoundé during the colonial period.

name: Route de Kiiki Scenic Area
shortDescription: A rural landscape route listed as a Centre Region tourist site.
fullDescription: The Kiiki route passes through the Mbam-et-Inoubou countryside and can be incorporated into excursions focused on rural landscapes and local communities.
funFact: It is included in the Ministry of Tourism's Centre Region attraction inventory.

name: Boumba-Bek National Park
shortDescription: A vast rainforest park in southeastern Cameroon.
fullDescription: Boumba-Bek protects dense Congo Basin rainforest and forms part of the country's major forest conservation landscape, with elephants, gorillas, and other wildlife.
funFact: The park is part of the wider forest complex of southeastern Cameroon.
openingHours: Guided visits only; arrange well in advance

name: Nki National Park
shortDescription: Remote rainforest wilderness in southeastern Cameroon.
fullDescription: Nki is a large protected rainforest area known for its biodiversity and remote forest landscapes, especially suited to specialist ecotourism.
funFact: Nki is among the protected areas included on Cameroon's UNESCO Tentative List as part of the Boumba-Bek and Nki complex.
openingHours: Guided expeditions only; arrange in advance

name: Sangha Trinational Forest Landscape
shortDescription: A transboundary rainforest conservation landscape.
fullDescription: The Sangha Trinational links protected forests across Cameroon, Central African Republic, and Republic of the Congo and is renowned for exceptional Congo Basin biodiversity.
funFact: The site is a UNESCO World Heritage property shared by three countries.
openingHours: Guided specialist visits; advance arrangements required

name: Lake Municipal of Garoua-Boulaï
shortDescription: A local lake and leisure landscape near the Central African border.
fullDescription: The municipal lake of Garoua-Boulaï is listed by the Ministry of Tourism as an attraction in the East Region and offers a quiet waterside setting.
funFact: It is one of the few specifically listed municipal tourist sites in the East Region.

name: Bertoua Cultural District
shortDescription: A gateway to the Gbaya and Maka cultural traditions.
fullDescription: Bertoua is a useful base for discovering eastern Cameroon culture, crafts, music, and regional traditions through local cultural venues and markets.
funFact: The East Region is particularly associated with Gbaya and Maka cultural heritage.

name: Baka Forest Ecotourism Area
shortDescription: Community-based encounters with Baka forest heritage.
fullDescription: Selected community-led forest experiences in southeastern Cameroon can introduce visitors to Baka knowledge, forest foods, crafts, and traditional ecological practices.
funFact: Responsible visits should be organized through local communities and avoid treating cultural practices as spectacles.

name: Dja River Landscapes
shortDescription: River landscapes surrounding the Dja rainforest.
fullDescription: The Dja River forms a striking natural boundary around much of the Dja Faunal Reserve and offers a way to appreciate the scale of the surrounding rainforest.
funFact: The reserve is almost entirely surrounded by the Dja River.

name: Moloundou Rainforest Gateway
shortDescription: A remote gateway to southeastern Cameroon's rainforest.
fullDescription: Moloundou is a starting point for journeys toward the forest reserves and communities of the Boumba-et-Ngoko area.
funFact: Its location makes it an important access point for southeastern forest excursions.

name: Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape
shortDescription: Ancient dry-stone archaeological sites in the Mandara Mountains.
fullDescription: Diy-Gid-Biy includes sixteen archaeological sites across seven villages, with dry-stone structures, terraces, tombs, and sacred places associated with long-standing Mafa settlement.
funFact: The archaeological structures are thought to date from roughly the 12th to 17th centuries.
openingHours: Guided cultural visit; confirm local access

name: Goulfey Sultanate Palace
shortDescription: Historic traditional palace in the Logone-Chari area.
fullDescription: The palace of Goulfey is part of the region's network of traditional sultanates and reflects the history and architecture of the Chadian Basin.
funFact: It is listed among the Far North's official tourist attractions.

name: Pouss Musgum Houses
shortDescription: Iconic earthen architecture of the Musgum people.
fullDescription: Pouss is known for its distinctive Musgum earthen houses, whose sculpted forms and decorative patterns are adapted to the region's climate and cultural traditions.
funFact: The famous shell-shaped houses are built from earth using traditional techniques.

name: Lake Maga
shortDescription: A large lake and wetland landscape in the Far North.
fullDescription: Lake Maga is an important water landscape near Yagoua and provides opportunities for birdwatching, fishing-related cultural experiences, and scenic outings.
funFact: The lake is closely connected to the irrigated agricultural landscape of the Logone plain.

name: Mozogo-Gokoro National Park
shortDescription: A protected woodland area in the Mandara region.
fullDescription: Mozogo-Gokoro protects a distinctive Sahelian woodland ecosystem and is one of the national parks highlighted in official descriptions of the Far North.
funFact: It is one of three national parks cited by the Cameroonian government in the region.

name: Kalamaloué National Park
shortDescription: A protected wetland and savanna area near Kousseri.
fullDescription: Kalamaloué lies near the Chari River and protects wildlife habitats in the northern floodplain landscape.
funFact: It is one of the national parks officially identified in the Far North Region.
openingHours: Guided visits; seasonal access may vary

name: Mindif Peak
shortDescription: A striking isolated mountain rising from the Far North plains.
fullDescription: The Pic de Mindif is a prominent rocky landmark in the Mayo-Kani area and offers dramatic views of the surrounding Sahelian landscape.
funFact: It is specifically listed by the Ministry of Tourism as a tourist site.

name: Lake Boboyo
shortDescription: A quiet lake landscape in Mayo-Kani.
fullDescription: Lake Boboyo is a lesser-known natural attraction in the Far North and offers a peaceful setting away from the larger safari destinations.
funFact: It is included in the official Far North tourism inventory.

name: Ekom-Nkam Falls
shortDescription: A spectacular waterfall in the Moungo area.
fullDescription: The Nkam and Oham rivers form the dramatic Ekom-Nkam waterfall, surrounded by dense vegetation and reached by a developed visitor trail.
funFact: The main waterfall is about 80 metres high and was used as a filming location for Greystoke.

name: Palace of the Bell Kings
shortDescription: Historic royal heritage site in Douala.
fullDescription: The Palace of the Bell Kings reflects the history of the Duala people and the traditional leadership structures of the Wouri estuary.
funFact: It is one of the sites listed by the Ministry of Tourism in Douala.

name: Place Joss
shortDescription: Historic urban square in Douala.
fullDescription: Place Joss is part of Douala's historic urban heritage and can be combined with visits to nearby colonial-era buildings and cultural landmarks.
funFact: The site appears in the Ministry of Tourism's official Douala attraction list.

name: Yoyo Beach
shortDescription: A coastal beach destination near Edéa.
fullDescription: Yoyo offers a quieter Atlantic coastal setting within the Littoral Region, away from central Douala.
funFact: It is listed by the Ministry of Tourism as a Littoral tourist site.
openingHours: Daylight hours; observe local sea conditions

name: Lake Ossa Wildlife Reserve
shortDescription: A lake and forest reserve near Edéa.
fullDescription: Lake Ossa combines inland waters, forest, and wildlife habitats and is an attractive option for nature and birdwatching excursions in the Littoral Region.
funFact: The reserve protects a distinctive freshwater lake ecosystem.

name: Manoka Island
shortDescription: An island community in the Wouri estuary.
fullDescription: Manoka offers a glimpse of coastal Sawa life, mangrove landscapes, fishing communities, and waterways around Douala.
funFact: The island is reached by boat and is best experienced with local community guidance.

name: Mouanko Coastal Area
shortDescription: Coastal landscapes and fishing communities around Mouanko.
fullDescription: Mouanko provides access to coastal scenery, estuaries, fishing villages, and the wider Douala-Edéa wetland environment.
funFact: The area is associated with mangroves and coastal ecosystems of the Sanaga Maritime.

name: Douala Historic Courthouse
shortDescription: Historic civic architecture in central Douala.
fullDescription: The historic courthouse is part of Douala's built heritage and can be visited as part of a walking route through the city's older administrative quarter.
funFact: It appears in the Ministry of Tourism's list of Wouri Department tourist sites.

name: Bouba Ndjida National Park
shortDescription: A major savanna wildlife park in northern Cameroon.
fullDescription: Bouba Ndjida protects extensive savanna and is known for elephants, lions, buffalo, and other wildlife of northern Cameroon.
funFact: The park is one of the three major protected areas highlighted for the North Region.

name: Faro National Park
shortDescription: A rugged savanna park along the Faro River.
fullDescription: Faro National Park protects savanna, gallery forest, and wildlife in the northern highlands and is a destination for specialist safari trips.
funFact: It is one of the three major national parks of the North Region.

name: Kola Gorges
shortDescription: A spectacular canyon near Guider.
fullDescription: The Kola Gorges form a four-kilometre canyon with caves, waterfalls, polished rock walls, and hiking routes that are best visited when water levels are low.
funFact: The gorge can reach depths of several hundred metres in places and contains a cave and waterfall.

name: Banks of the Benoué River
shortDescription: A riverside leisure and wildlife-viewing area in Garoua.
fullDescription: The developed riverfront offers views over the Benoué, with nearby wetlands and pools where hippopotamuses can sometimes be observed.
funFact: The Benoué eventually joins the Niger River in Nigeria.

name: Baschéo Tourist Camp
shortDescription: A northern savanna base for outdoor excursions.
fullDescription: The Baschéo tourist camp is listed among the official tourism sites of the North Region and provides a base for exploring the surrounding landscape.
funFact: It is located in the Bénoué Department.

name: Demsa Horse Museum
shortDescription: A museum celebrating horse culture and the local Lamidat tradition.
fullDescription: The Demsa horse museum presents aspects of northern Cameroon's equestrian heritage and the history of the local traditional leadership.
funFact: The museum was established in 2007 and includes links to horse-riding traditions.

name: Lamidat of Garoua
shortDescription: Traditional Fulani leadership heritage in Garoua.
fullDescription: The Lamidat of Garoua offers a cultural perspective on traditional authority, architecture, ceremonies, and the history of the city.
funFact: Lamidats remain living cultural institutions rather than historical monuments only.

name: Mayo-Rey Dinosaur Track Sites
shortDescription: Fossil track sites in northern Cameroon.
fullDescription: The Mayo-Rey area contains fossilized dinosaur footprints and is recognized by the Ministry of Tourism as an important paleontological attraction.
funFact: The fossil tracks are among Cameroon's unusual links to prehistoric landscapes.
openingHours: Guided visit; arrange with local authorities

name: Lake Oku
shortDescription: A high-altitude crater lake beneath Mount Oku.
fullDescription: Lake Oku sits in the volcanic highlands of the Northwest and is surrounded by forest and mountain scenery.
funFact: It is one of the region's well-known crater lakes and lies near Mount Oku.

name: Lake Awing
shortDescription: A scenic crater lake surrounded by highlands.
fullDescription: Lake Awing offers a peaceful landscape of water, rolling hills, and local farming communities and is well suited to photography and nature walks.
funFact: The lake is among the water bodies identified by Cameroon's regional planning authorities as having tourism potential.

name: Menchum Falls
shortDescription: A powerful waterfall in the Menchum highlands.
fullDescription: Menchum Falls drops through a dramatic forested landscape and is one of the Northwest's most famous natural landmarks.
funFact: The falls are repeatedly identified as a major tourism asset of the Northwest Region.

name: Kilum-Ijim Forest
shortDescription: A highland forest famous for rare birds and biodiversity.
fullDescription: Kilum-Ijim is one of the most important remaining mountain forests in the Northwest and is associated with the endangered Bannerman's turaco.
funFact: The forest is one of the key habitats of the Bannerman's turaco.
openingHours: Guided ecological visit; arrange in advance

name: Lake Bambili
shortDescription: A volcanic lake near Bambili.
fullDescription: Lake Bambili is a scenic highland water body surrounded by volcanic terrain and local settlements.
funFact: Regional planning documents identify Lake Bambili as a tourism site.

name: Mbengwi Caves
shortDescription: Cave landscapes in the Momo area.
fullDescription: The Mbengwi caves are among the natural attractions identified in the Northwest and offer an underground adventure for visitors accompanied by local guides.
funFact: The caves are mentioned alongside the region's lakes and waterfalls in tourism planning material.
openingHours: Guided visit only; suitable equipment recommended

name: Mankon Museum
shortDescription: A cultural museum preserving Mankon heritage.
fullDescription: The Mankon museum is associated with the cultural heritage of the Mankon people and traditional arts of the Bamenda area.
funFact: UNESCO included the museum in heritage assessments of the Northwest's cultural assets.

name: Ndawara Tea Estates
shortDescription: Highland tea plantations with scenic views.
fullDescription: The Ndawara area is known for highland tea cultivation, rolling landscapes, and cool mountain scenery.
funFact: The tea estates are among the Northwest's recognizable agricultural landscapes.

name: Ekom-Nkam Falls – West Approach
shortDescription: The West Region's approach to the famous Ekom-Nkam waterfall.
fullDescription: The waterfall sits on the Nkam area associated with the boundary between the West and Littoral regions; the West-side approach passes through lush highland vegetation.
funFact: Ekom-Nkam is around 80 metres high and has been used as a film location.

name: Fovu Cave
shortDescription: A natural cave and rock formation in the West highlands.
fullDescription: Fovu is a striking natural formation associated with the Baham area and is suited to short adventure excursions and local cultural interpretation.
funFact: It is included among the natural and leisure sites promoted by the West Regional tourism office.

name: Lake Baleng
shortDescription: A volcanic lake in the Bafoussam highlands.
fullDescription: Lake Baleng is surrounded by highland scenery and offers a calm setting for nature walks, photography, and cultural discovery.
funFact: The lake is listed among the West Region's natural attractions.

name: Lake Bamendjing
shortDescription: A scenic highland lake and reservoir landscape.
fullDescription: Bamendjing provides expansive water views amid the West Region's rolling volcanic highlands.
funFact: It is included in the West Regional tourism office's list of natural sites and leisure destinations.
openingHours: Daylight hours; observe local water-safety guidance

name: Bana Royal Palace
shortDescription: Traditional royal heritage of the Bana kingdom.
fullDescription: The Bana palace and chiefdom area showcase Bamileke architecture, royal traditions, and craftsmanship in the West Region.
funFact: Bana is known for distinctive royal architecture and cultural heritage.

name: Bangou Museographic Village
shortDescription: A cultural heritage site presenting local traditions.
fullDescription: The Bangou museographic village preserves and presents elements of local material culture, architecture, and traditions of the West Region.
funFact: It is listed in the Ministry of Tourism's national tourist-site inventory.
openingHours: By guided visit; confirm hours locally

name: Mouankeu Falls
shortDescription: A waterfall near Bafang in the Haut-Nkam.
fullDescription: Mouankeu Falls is a natural attraction surrounded by the lush landscapes of the Haut-Nkam Department and is suited to short nature excursions.
funFact: The falls are officially listed by the Ministry of Tourism among West Region attractions.

name: Foréké-Dschang Cliff
shortDescription: A dramatic highland escarpment near Dschang.
fullDescription: The Foréké-Dschang cliff offers panoramic views and a striking example of the volcanic and mountainous landscapes of the West Region.
funFact: It is promoted by the West Regional tourism office as a natural and leisure site.

name: Ebodjè Ecotourism Site
shortDescription: A fishing village known for sea-turtle conservation.
fullDescription: Ebodjè combines beaches, canoe excursions, forest scenery, and community-based turtle conservation on Cameroon's southern coast.
funFact: Marine turtles come to the beach to lay eggs especially from November to January.

name: Grand Batanga Beach
shortDescription: A broad Atlantic beach south of Kribi.
fullDescription: Grand Batanga offers coastal scenery, fishing culture, and a quieter beach experience near Kribi.
funFact: The beach is one of the coastal sites listed by Cameroon's Ministry of Tourism.

name: Campo Beach
shortDescription: A scenic beach near the Campo area.
fullDescription: Campo's coast combines Atlantic beaches with rainforest landscapes and access to the Campo Ma'an area.
funFact: The beach is officially listed among South Region tourist sites.
openingHours: Daylight hours; observe local sea conditions

name: Dja River Banks
shortDescription: River landscapes around Sangmélima and Dja-et-Lobo.
fullDescription: The banks of the Dja provide opportunities for nature outings and a different perspective on the forested interior of the South Region.
funFact: The site is listed in the Ministry of Tourism's South Region attraction inventory.

name: Living Museum of Dja-et-Lobo
shortDescription: A cultural attraction presenting local traditions.
fullDescription: The Living Museum in the Dja-et-Lobo area offers visitors an opportunity to encounter local material culture and heritage in a community-oriented setting.
funFact: It is officially listed among the South Region's tourist sites.

name: Ako-Okas Rock Massif
shortDescription: A dramatic twin-rock formation near Ebolowa.
fullDescription: Ako-Okas, sometimes called the mystical python, is a prominent rock massif where visitors can hike and discover Bulu cultural landscapes and cocoa-growing areas.
funFact: The higher rock formations rise to around 800 metres above their surroundings.

name: Dja River Riverside Landscapes
shortDescription: Scenic river landscapes around Sangmélima.
fullDescription: The Dja riverside area offers forest scenery and quiet river views in the interior of the South Region.
funFact: The riverside is included in the Ministry of Tourism's official South Region inventory.

name: Kribi Lighthouse
shortDescription: Historic coastal lighthouse overlooking the Atlantic.
fullDescription: The Kribi lighthouse is a recognizable landmark of the coastal city and a reminder of the town's maritime and colonial-era history.
funFact: The lighthouse dates to the German colonial period and remains one of Kribi's visual landmarks.
openingHours: Viewable from outside; confirm interior access

name: Bimbia Heritage Site
shortDescription: A historic coastal site connected to the Atlantic slave trade.
fullDescription: Bimbia preserves remnants of a former coastal trading settlement and is a major place for learning about Cameroon's Atlantic and colonial history.
funFact: The site includes a historic 'Door of No Return' area associated with the slave-trade history of the coast.
openingHours: Guided heritage visit; confirm current access

name: German Cannon of Bimbia
shortDescription: A surviving colonial-era military artifact at Bimbia.
fullDescription: The German cannon is one of the tangible historical remains associated with Bimbia and can be combined with a heritage visit to the site.
funFact: It is listed by the Ministry of Tourism among Southwest tourist attractions.

name: Limbe Wildlife Centre
shortDescription: A wildlife rescue and conservation centre in Limbe.
fullDescription: The centre focuses on the care and conservation of primates and other wildlife and provides an accessible introduction to Cameroon's forest fauna.
funFact: It is one of Limbe's best-known wildlife attractions.

name: Down Beach Limbe
shortDescription: A black-sand coastal beach in Limbe.
fullDescription: Down Beach combines volcanic coastal scenery with fishing activity and views across the Gulf of Guinea.
funFact: The dark sand reflects the volcanic geology of the Mount Cameroon area.

name: Twin Lakes of Manenguba
shortDescription: High-altitude twin crater lakes on Mount Manenguba.
fullDescription: The two lakes sit in a spectacular mountain setting and are reached by hiking routes through the highlands.
funFact: The Ministry of Tourism notes that the female lake is considered dangerous and inaccessible; the male lake is the usual visitor destination.
openingHours: Daylight hours; guided mountain visit strongly recommended

name: Bakossi National Park
shortDescription: A rainforest and mountain park in the Koupé-Manengouba area.
fullDescription: Bakossi protects montane and lowland forest habitats with exceptional plant and wildlife diversity.
funFact: The park is officially listed among the Southwest Region's ecotourism attractions.
openingHours: Guided visits only; arrange in advance

name: Bakingili Black-Sand Beach
shortDescription: A volcanic black-sand beach west of Limbe.
fullDescription: Bakingili's coastline combines dark volcanic sand, Atlantic views, and the dramatic backdrop of Mount Cameroon.
funFact: The beach landscape reflects the region's volcanic geology.

name: Buea Historic Colonial Quarter
shortDescription: Historic buildings and landscapes around Buea's old administrative area.
fullDescription: Buea's historic quarter preserves traces of the German and later colonial periods at the foot of Mount Cameroon.
funFact: The town served as the capital of German Kamerun for a period during the colonial era.
openingHours: Viewable outdoors; guided heritage walk recommended
